newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telefonica eyes further Brazil investment.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica eyes further Brazil investment.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana wants to invest further in Brazilian telecoms and hopes to do so through new partner Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT), the company's chief said.

"We are interested in the privatization of Telebras and other opportunities which might come up (in Brazil)," said Marcial Portela, president of Telefonica's overseas arm Telefonica Internacional S.A. (TISA).
Whether or not the firm invests on its own through TISA or through CRT will largely depend on the pace of Brazil's privatization program, he said.

The Brazilian government plans to privatize Brazil's massive telecommunications sector, starting next year with the break up and partial sale of federal giant Telebras. It also intends in mid-1997 to begin granting concessions for firms to operate on the B Band cellular frequency. Both have drawn the interest of the world's largest telecom operators.

Telefonica is operating partner in a group that Tuesday bought a strategic 35 percent stake in CRT, which is majority owned by Rio Grande do Sul state, in the first opening of the sector to private capital.

Portela said it is too early to say how much Telefonica or the group will invest in CRT, but suggested it would be in the hundreds of millions of dollars. But he said the market and the telephone company's size are "very similar" to those of Chile, when Telefonica bought that country's state telecom in 1991 and could require similar spending.
Over the past five years, Telefonica has invested an average $500 million a year in Cia de Telecomunicaciones de Chile (CTC), he said.
Telefonica de Espana teamed with Brazil's RBS Participacoes, Telefonica de Argentina, CTC and Citicorp to buy the CRT stake.
Portela said the group's members may alter their interest in the consortium as Citicorp is studying the legal ramifications of expanding its participation to 14 percent from one percent.
RBS's stake would then change to 34 percent, while 52 percent would be owned by Telefonica de Espana, Telefonica de Argentina and CTC, he said.
He did not say how much each now holds in the consortium.
The state has retained 51-percent control of CRT, but the Telefonica-led group will be strategic-operating partner.
